AmbientState.description:
The "main player" lane. Holds the current track, what's coming up,
and what's already played (for skip_prev). `position_ms` is the server's
best guess of where in the current track playback is — updated by user
actions (play/seek/skip) and by position reports from the active output.

While an interrupt is active, `position_ms` is *not* updated (position
reports go to the interrupt lane), so it preserves the resume point
automatically.

`shuffle` controls how `skip_next` picks the next track: "off" advances
sequentially (queue head); "random" pulls a random queue entry.
AmbientState.title: AmbientState

ApplyRequest.description:
One chunk of accepted operations. The client slices a big apply into

BulkMetadataResult.description:
Bulk-update result. `updated` is the rows that took the change;
`skipped` is the per-track failures (file missing, format we can't
write tags for, …) so the operator sees which tracks didn't apply
instead of silently swallowing the discrepancy.
BulkMetadataResult.title: BulkMetadataResult

BulkMetadataUpdate.description:

skipped — only fields the caller explicitly sets are touched. To clear
a field across a selection, send the empty string explicitly.
BulkMetadataUpdate.title: BulkMetadataUpdate

InterruptState.description:
An interrupt is a short audio override. Its lifecycle ends either by
queue exhaustion (auto-completion via `interrupt_skip_next` past the end)
or explicit cancel. On completion, behavior depends on
`return_to_ambient`: true → ambient takes back over from its preserved
position; false → playback stops.

`duck_to` controls how ambient behaves *during* the interrupt:
- `None` (default): ambient pauses - full cut, position frozen.
- `0.0`..`1.0`: ambient keeps playing at this multiplier relative to the
  device's output level, creating a cinematic duck. Same fade
  durations as the interrupt's fade_in/out drive the ramp.
InterruptState.title: InterruptState

LoaderStatus.description:
Snapshot of the most recent load_all run for modes or presets.
`loaded_ids` and `errors` reflect the state as of `last_load_at`.
Both empty + `last_load_at == None` means load_all hasn't run yet
(boot still in progress, or the seed dirs were empty).
LoaderStatus.title: LoaderStatus

LoopingSfx.description:
A repeating SFX driven by a server-side interval timer. Held in
PlayerState so every client's LOOPS panel shows the same live set; the
actual timers live in `sync/loops.py`. `id` is the stop handle.
LoopingSfx.title: LoopingSfx

PlayerState.description: Canonical playback state. The server is the sole writer.

TrackMetadataUpdate.description:
Mixed bag: tag-backed fields are written to the file's ID3/Vorbis

VerifyRequest.description:

(the lookup client paces at 1 request/second, two queries per name) so
a synchronous call stays well under proxy timeouts; the client chunks
a longer list and shows progress between calls.
VerifyRequest.title: VerifyRequest

Every remembered device, including offline ones — the whole point is to

delete.description:
Forget a device — drop it from the saved list (so it no longer
auto-activates by default). If it's still connected it remains usable and,
if it was a live output, keeps playing this session until turned off.

put.description:
Remember a device (the manual 'save'/'add'), or update an existing one's
name / default-on designation. Idempotent create-or-update.

`is_output` here is the "output by default" flag: it controls whether the
device auto-activates as a live output when it next connects — it does NOT
gate or change the *current* live active set. Toggling it on/off only
affects future connects (and the badge in the footer); a device that's
live right now keeps playing until it's turned off from the Speakers
popover or disconnects. (Activation is independent — any connected device
can be ticked on without being saved.)

matching the single-track endpoint.

post.description:
Delete many tracks at once. A missing file isn't fatal — the row is
still dropped from the index so the operator can clean up dangling rows
after manually removing files. Playlist items cascade via FK.

patch.description:
Apply the same metadata update across many tracks at once.

Tag-backed fields are written to each file's tags (and a re-scan picks
them back up); DB-only fields (`display_title`, `origin`) are set
directly on the row. Files that no longer exist on disk OR can't be
written are reported in `skipped` with a reason — the operator sees
exactly which tracks didn't take the change. DB-only fields apply
unconditionally since they don't read from disk.

post.description:
Move many tracks to one destination folder, keeping their original
filenames. Per-track failures (missing source, name collision, etc.) are
collected into `skipped` so the operator sees exactly what didn't move,
rather than the whole batch aborting on the first issue.

delete.description:
Delete the file from disk AND the row from the index. Any playlist
items referencing this track id cascade-delete (FK on playlist_items).

get.description:
Single-track metadata. Open to guests so a logged-out Player tab
(e.g. a bookmarked TV display) can show what's playing.
Cover art. Guest-accessible — Player tab needs it for the room display.

patch.description:
Edit metadata for a single track. Tag-backed fields go to the
underlying file's tags (and the row is re-indexed from disk); DB-only
fields are written straight to the row. Only fields explicitly set in

post.description:
Move the file to another folder under MUSIC_DIR, optionally with a new
filename. The disk move and the index update are kept consistent: if the
DB update raises after the file is moved, we attempt to move the file
back before surfacing the error so the index and the filesystem don't
drift.
